notes: EVERY DEATH MORE THAN 3 BLOCKS BELOW THE RECENT PEAK CRASHED THE BOT. index.mjs read `cause` in `fallRecord(..., { cause: deathClass(cause) })` five lines above `const cause = freshDeathCause()` (8f1e037, live since 859af48 on 09-27). The temporal-dead-zone ReferenceError threw out of mineflayer's health.js packet handler and killed the process (journal: index.mjs:1002:94, exit 1): 17 crashes on 15 bots in 36 h. The restarted bot rejoins dead and logs the death again as 'unknown; idle', so the death COUNT survived (17 of 17 crashes matched to such a row ~11 s later) and the cause, fall distance and death site did not: `after falling` rows went from 6-45 a day on every build through efa2853 to 0 of 60 on 859af48 and later. The fall-class death-tripper went blind. THE CHANGE: the declaration moves above the read; hpTrail is cleared after the death record (a ring that spanned lives, which the restart hid). test/no-tdz.test.mjs runs ESLint no-use-before-define over src/, found exactly this site and failed before the fix. Reviewed by Claude and Codex (both confirmed the fix; they disagreed on the gate and the host settled it 17/17). SANDBOX 2026-09-28 13:52Z, same arena, 17-block drop: control 80b3bbd threw the ReferenceError and wrote no _death row; candidate wrote 'fell from a high place after falling 17 blocks'. WHY THE GATE IS CORRECTNESS: the fix is deterministic; the fleet question is only whether it ran and harmed nothing. EXPECT the death-tripper to see fall deaths again; compare to the 6-45/day baseline, not to zero.

licence.note: The baseline cannot write this text: it throws before the _death row on exactly the deaths that carry it (0 of 60 deaths on 859af48+). ~0.006 crash-class deaths per bot-hour, so ~3 expected on 20 canary bots in 26 h; min_rows 1 because this gates that the branch RAN, and P(0 | 3) is ~5%, in which case the run is INCONCLUSIVE, not wrong.

require.name: descent/injury rows (the population whose deaths this fix records)

draw_exposure.note: Every pool wrote 4-39 _fall_path rows in the 3 h before registration (hive-b lowest at 4); min 3 is a tripwire against a pool that has gone quiet, not a filter.

exposure.note: Ready = at least one canary after-falling death (the fix ran) AND at least one control crash (the crash instrument can see a presence). Expected ~0.7 canary fall deaths and ~2 control crashes per 6 h, hence the extension.

own_lines.note: CORRECTNESS. One ReferenceError crash on a canary unit means the fix did not fix it. Deterministic.

POSITIVE CONTROL for the journal query: ~9 expected in control over 26 h (dry run over 24 h on 69 control-equivalent bots found 9). A control zero means the instrument could not see a crash, so a canary zero proves nothing. No evidence class: BLOCKS KEEP, never reverts.
INSTRUMENT. A journalctl call that failed is a unit not checked. No evidence class: BLOCKS KEEP.
The baseline cannot write 'after falling'. A control row means the arms are wrong. No evidence class: BLOCKS KEEP.
LIVENESS. Zero means the fixed handler never ran on the fleet. No evidence class: BLOCKS KEEP (INCONCLUSIVE), never reverts.

COVERAGE (Codex review). Units come from systemd, and every canary pool must field 5; a missing unit is a unit whose crashes were never checked. Positive control: a nonexistent pool reads 5 missing. No evidence class: BLOCKS KEEP.
COVERAGE (Codex review). A running bot logs every few minutes, so a successful journal query with NO lines saw nothing. No evidence class: BLOCKS KEEP.

primary.note: REPORTED, NOT GATED. The 'unknown; idle' re-count rows should fall on the canary because no restart follows these deaths; the dry run over 24 h found them equal to the journal crashes (3 and 9).

harm.note: Unchanged: the two-death floor (OWNER 2026-09-11) and gather_ratio < 0.43 of control. Death COUNTS are unchanged by this fix (the baseline re-counts after the restart), so any canary excess is real, not an artefact of better labels.

teardown.note: THREE STEPS: drop-ins, clear canary_pool, restart the pool's bots 12 s apart; then confirm the live versions.

amendments.what: Codex review of the staged canary: units from systemd instead of log directories; two coverage gates added; fall rows version-bound to the canary build
why: 88 log directories exist for 80 bots, so directory enumeration could misattribute or skip; a missing unit or an empty successful journal query could pass silently.

Promotion safety verified on the host: verdict.py returns NOT_YET below max(read_minutes) (line 1069), KEEP only at the final read with every line passing, a blocked line gives INCONCLUSIVE, and only the KEEP branch of canary-loop.sh promotes.

amendments.what: OWNER DECISION "shorten the canary for fixes": reads 180/360 + extension until exposure (540/720/1080/1560); exposure = exposure_ready

exposure.note: One recorded after-falling death on the canary shows the fixed handler ran on the fleet.

extension.note: SHORT CANARY for a fix (owner 2026-09-29). KEEP is possible from +360 when correctness, harm and exposure are all clean; without exposure the loop keeps reading at 540/720/1080/1560 and calls INCONCLUSIVE only at the last.
